newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Soldier from Turk side shot dead in Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Soldier from Turk side shot dead in Cyprus.

text.p: A soldier from the Turkish side of the divided island of Cyprus was shot dead on Sunday near the United Nations-patrolled buffer zone that separates Greek and Turkish Cypriots, British military officials said.
It was not immediately clear who was responsible for the shooting.

The Turkish foreign ministry in Ankara confirmed a report issued by the state-run Anatolian news agency that a Turkish Cypriot soldier was shot dead by Greek Cypriots, but British military officials on the island said it was unclear what had happened.
Greek Cypriot police said they did not have any information about the incident.

The shooting -- in which Anatolian said another Turkish Cypriot soldier was wounded -- occurred about 4 a.m. (0100 GMT) at a Turkish Cypriot guard unit in Acheritou village, which Turks call Guvercinlik, on the northern edge of the British base of Dhekelia in south eastern Cyprus.
"A Turkish soldier was shot and killed about two miles east of Ayios Nicolaos," said Captain Sean Tully, spokesman for the British bases in Cyprus.
Ayios Nicolaos, base of the 9th Signals Regiment, is an area on the northern edge of Dhekelia base.
"The Sovereign Base Police (SBA) are there investigating the incident with the United Nations," said Tully. "So far the incident is shrouded in mystery."
"We have nothing whatsoever," said a spokesman for Cyprus police.

Tensions have risen in the last month following the killing of two Greek Cypriots by security forces and civilians in the Turkish-occupied areas during demonstrations against the division of the island.
The island has been virtually partitioned since Turkish troops invaded 22 years ago after a short-lived coup engineered by the military regime then ruling Greece.
Only Turkey recognises a breakaway Turkish Cypriot state set up in the north of the island in 1983.
Some 30,000 mainland Turkish troops are stationed there, and the protracted dispute is a source of tension between Turkey and Greece, its neighbour and NATO partner.
A senior aide to U.S. President Bill Clinton said on Thursday that Washington would push forward with its initiative to help reunite the divided island.
